note: Hand-maintained ledger of filed klayout-tools friction issues; see README.md 'klayout-tools friction ledger'. Gate: .github/scripts/check-klt-friction.sh

entries.gap: Extraction deck recognises no SiGe HBT (bipolar) devices.
Documentation of why SiGe HBTs are not recognised by the extraction deck.
Composition router: a cross-block via drop can short an unrelated net without any routed/unrouted/warning signal (cited here for the router's pin-approach-side behaviour).
Generator cannot reach the PDK's PCell library from the tool's Python path (compat shim not on sys.path; GUI-toolkit crash in the vendor shim).
Signoff tier item for power delivery (structural) added.
Signoff tier report names its checklist but does not pin the checklist content.
With an external tiers doc, the doc's item list and the build's grading logic can diverge silently.
Design spike for ERC well/substrate-tap net continuity.
Signoff report lacked per-item build-grading coverage and the build name.
ERC has no declarable tap for an implant-free stream, so the missing-tie half of the power-delivery item is unreachable for full-custom analog.
Simulation requests cannot express an OSDI device, an ngspice compatibility mode, a save policy, or a multi-library corner axis.
Curated deck's poly-resistor body/marker roles are inverted relative to the PDK's own PCell convention, so no drawn poly resistor is recognised.
Curated DRC contact rule drops the active-mask join, so every HBT contact false-positives.
External-deck DRC engine cannot use the bundled KLayout and does not preflight the PATH one's DSL feature level.
Ring continuity check cannot scope its layer set, so a shared layer can report continuous from unrelated geometry.
Zero-finding external-deck DRC runs can never be labelled clean; needs an opt-in coverage assertion.
Router via drops use a fixed contact constant that violates PDKs whose via rules are min-and-max.
No independent way to derive or check the expected rule-category set of an external-deck DRC run (count-only, input-dependent).
No device-aware LVS path when a PDK's own LVS runset recognises devices the curated deck lacks (no native-runset engine).
Extract writes its default netlist next to the input stream, so a read-only run drops a file into the source tree.
Batch simulation: runner/client tool version mismatch surfaces only after instance launch as per-corner errors; no override or preflight.
Tiers: accept a PDK-runset LVS report as evidence for the LVS items (depends on the native-runset LVS gap).
Batch simulation: request features newer than the fleet runner fail the whole job instead of being refused client-side.
Signoff: no evidence form for the generator/netlist-freshness items (directory of committed artifacts).
Batch runner older than the client silently drops newer request options under a warn-only version check.
